verdict.reasoning: Patient reports numbness, tingling, and mild weakness of the left arm for about two weeks: "I'd say for at least two weeks and it's kind of gotten worse... tingling and then it's gotten worse... then the numbing kind of started" and later agrees there is "mild" weakness.

She links onset to starting boxing: "I've started taking this boxing class. I've been taking boxing class for a few weeks and I feel like maybe it's probably been, I'd say for at least two weeks" referring to her symptoms.

She describes initial tingling progressing to numbness from elbow down: "I just kind of felt a little bit of tingling and then it's gotten worse since then. Then the numbing kind of started. I can feel it both in my... elbow and then in my arm as well as in my hand."
She specifies palmar involvement of digits 2–4: "it's my second, third and fourth finger" and clarifies "It's the front side" when asked if palm side or back of hand.
She notes shoulder pain with movement: "sometimes I will feel it in my shoulder. Like if I try to... move like in boxing and stuff, I will even like maybe feel a little bit of... pain."

She has mild fine motor difficulty but can still grasp: "I play a little bit of a piano and so I just noticed that it's... harder to get the notes... I can grasp a glass..." and agrees to mild weakness.
She reports using massage and warm baths without benefit: "I tried massage, I tried some hot baths and that didn't help with this numbness."

She had transient left visual field loss: "I all of a sudden just couldn't see from... my left eye. Like, I lost some, like a little bit of a field of vision" and later: "I think it was only maybe like 20 minutes or so."
She acknowledges occasional headaches: "Sometimes I get headaches, but I think they're just tired headaches."
She explicitly denies neck pain: Doctor: "Any neck pain at all?" Patient: "No, not. No neck pain."
She denies seizures: Doctor explains seizures then asks; patient responds, "Oh, no, no, no, no. Nothing like that."
She confirms normal walking: Doctor: "your weakness is only in your left arm, leg, walking and all this. Normal?" Patient: "Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. Walking is normal."

She describes a flu-like illness about a month ago lasting about two weeks: "a really bad cold like a month ago" and "I was sick for probably good, like, two weeks... I think I must have had some kind of like a flu or something."

She links heavy alcohol use to that illness period: "I was out, you know, drinking with friends... we kind of went crazy and we were like out partying until... late hours, and I just got uncharacteristically drunk for me. And then after that, I was sick..."
She states ibuprofen use: "I do take ibuprofen just because my muscles were sore a little bit... I've just kind of taken ibuprofen for that."
She reports vitamin D use: "Not really. I just take ibuprofen every once in a while I take vitamin D."
She reports melatonin use: "And then sometimes I take melatonin to help me sleep."
She describes intermittent iron use with poor adherence: "my GP really wants me to take iron supplements, but you know, there are this like huge pill, so I, most of the time I just forget."
She reports father's thyroid/autoimmune issues: "I know that my dad has. I don't know if it's hypo. I think it's hypothyroidism... he's got some autoimmune stuff going on."
She lists mother's conditions: "my mom... she's got diabetes, type 2, she's got hypertension, she's got... high cholesterol."
She states she works out a lot: "In general, I'm pretty healthy. I mean, I, you know, I work out a lot" indicating regular exercise.
She clearly says she is taking boxing classes: "I've started taking this boxing class. I've been taking boxing class for a few weeks."

The assessment restates her history: left arm paresthesia and mild weakness for ~2 weeks, sensory distribution digits 2–4 palmar: supported by "for at least two weeks"; numbness/tingling and mild weakness; and "second, third and fourth finger" with palmar side involvement.
Assessment of a single transient left visual field episode matches: "I all of a sudden just couldn't see... lost some... field of vision" and "I think it was only maybe like 20 minutes or so."
Recent viral illness about one month prior is in HPI: "a really bad cold like a month ago" lasting two weeks and thought to be "some kind of like a flu or something."

Doctor expresses concern for MS: "Sometimes, you know, you do get things like ms, multiple sclerosis... people with multiple sclerosis can have visual problems like what you've experienced and sometimes... numbness, tingling" and calls it "the most serious kind of thing that needs to be dealt with," indicating concern for a central demyelinating process.

The doctor contrasts MS with "just like a boxing injury" but does not explicitly articulate a differential including peripheral/plexus injury or focal entrapment: "I'm just wondering whether there's something a bit more than just the box in here"; no detailed peripheral/traumatic differential is documented.
He explicitly plans an urgent neurology referral: "I'm going to do an urgent, very urgent neurology referral."
He anticipates neuroimaging: "What they... might entail is the brain scan and things like that," implying expedited brain imaging and further neurologic workup via neurology.

He declines starting steroids before diagnosis: "that's something we can't do. The treatment for it is actually some steroids... But saying that first we need... firm diagnosis." This indicates avoiding empiric steroids pre-diagnosis.

He gives explicit safety-net advice: "if the weakness progresses to your legs or there's any kind of headaches, vomiting, fits, and your visual symptoms are getting worse and not getting better, then that would be an A" (emergency), covering leg weakness, worsening vision, severe headache, vomiting, and seizures.

There is no instruction to continue ibuprofen or other symptomatic measures; ibuprofen is only mentioned as past/current use, not as part of the plan: "I do take ibuprofen..." with no directive from the doctor to continue it.
